Book a school tour for Foundation Stage (Reception) 2027 with the headteacher or deputy headteacher by emailing or calling the school office:
office@parkwoodprimary.org.uk
At our school, we pride ourselves on creating a calm and nurturing environment where every child can thrive. Our values drive our commitment to instilling respect, kindness, and empathy, ensuring that our children grow into considerate citizens. We believe in engaging our children positively, encouraging them to contribute meaningfully to our community. Our carefully considered curriculum is designed to spark curiosity and inspire through engaging and meaningful learning experiences. We tailor our teaching to meet the individual needs of our children, fostering confidence while providing the necessary challenges for them to reach their full potential. We are dedicated to cultivating self-assured, resilient, and ambitious learners, equipping them with the skills and mindset to flourish both academically and socially. We warmly invite you to explore our website and discover the opportunities we offer.
Mrs McCormack, Headteacher

We open at 7.30am in the external building situated on our front playground.
The following breakfast options are available: toast, cereal, yoghurts, fruit, water and squash. Food service will finish at 8.20am.
Staff will then escort children safely to the classrooms for the start of the school day.
Our service is available until 6.00pm. All children will receive a small snack e.g. biscuit with a drink on arrival. Those who stay beyond 4.15pm, will received a hot/cold snack. Hot snacks will include: beans on toast, soup and bread, jacket potato and hotdogs. Cold snacks include sandwiches or rolls. If parents arrive after this time, a charge will be issued to cover overtime costs owed to staff.
Arborwill be used to book your child into our wraparound care as and when you need it although your booking must be made 48 hours in advance so that we are able to ensure we have enough food for all children and to ensure we are adequately staffed. Payment will also be made through Arbor. Please see Ms Russell at the office to be added to the wraparound care service on Arbor.
If you use the government tax-free childcare service, you will need to let us know via the office email as we will need to set up Arbor differently for you.

Personal development is a school ethos. It is reflected in our school values (kind, honest, resilient, ambitious and responsible) as well as the way we encourage good behaviours (safe, respectful and ready).
Our aim is to teach children how to navigate through life safely, happily and healthily. Children are growing up in a world that is constantly changing and it is the duty of all the staff at school, in partnership with the parents and the wider community, to develop each child’s transferable life skills. We teach children about the world around them, relationships, emotions, reproduction and health, in order to prepare them for life in the modern world.

It is our intention that all children become successful, fluent readers who enjoy engaging in a wide range of texts. We understand the important role reading plays in the lives of our pupils and how it impacts on their learning in all other areas of the curriculum. We believe that learning to read is an essential part of every child’s education. Our reading curriculum starts with discrete teaching of synthetic phonics along side developing a love of reading, using high quality texts that are language rich. Parkwood Primary School prioritises the development of reading fluency and as our children become readers, they develop their thinking around and understanding of texts more deeply.

In addition to White Rose Maths teaching, Year 1 and Year 2 will be teaching an additional 10 minutes of maths teaching a day designed by the NCETM to build number sense. It is fully funded by the NCETM. FS will use a blend of the NCETM Number Sense scheme and White Rose. See overviews for Number Sense below.
For further information regarding the Number Sense scheme, use the link below:
https://www.ncetm.org.uk/maths-hubs-projects/mastering-number/
For Key Stage 1, we are using Numbots to support your child's understanding of number bonds and to help their addition and subtraction skills. These are essential building blocks for higher-level maths concepts. In order to get the best out of NumBots, we recommend that children play regularly for short bursts at a time, aiming for 3 minutes, five times a week.
We know how important it is to reduce cognitive load therefore we also invest in Times Tables Rock Stars. This program allows the children from year 2 upwards to rehearse their number facts and to memorise times tables makes it far quicker for children to work out mental maths problems in their heads. We recommended using Times Tables Rock Stars for 3 minutes a day because practise little and often will move this knowledge into our long term memories.

Our curriculum is designed in a way that means children 'work' like an expert in each subject. The curriculum is shaped through the use of questions that force teaching to include fundamental knowledge and skills required. For example, in art, the question 'How do people talk about art?' is used. This results in children learning about different ways that people interpret and talk about art e.g., Year 1 evaluate art with an understanding of how art can be varied and made in different ways by different people. year 5 are expected to consider how effectively a piece of art expresses emotion and creates atmosphere.
This is also achieved by carefully identifying key concepts to be revisited across the school. For example, the concept of 'environment' in geography is explored in Year 4 when the children study land use around the River Medway. Later in Year 6, they look at how natural disasters impact the people living where these disasters occur.
